payload.data: Taierzhuang, on the Grand Canal, 30 March 1938. For a week the Japanese have fought into the town. South of the canal the Chinese 10th Artillery has brought two German 15 cm sFH 18/32L howitzers, whose 15 km outranges every Japanese gun here.
No record says where the two Chinese 15 cm howitzers stood. The replay puts them south of Xiongshan, where the Japanese thought they were, beyond the reach of every Japanese gun.
On the map each battery's reach is drawn as a fan. A Japanese gunner later wrote: "a mere two Rheinmetalls completely suppressed our whole artillery".
03:00: about a thousand Chinese come north from the station along the railway against the Japanese reserve south of Sanlizhuang.
03:30: they reach the 2nd Heavy Company's guns north of Sanlizhuang and are driven off by fire at point-blank range.
06:00: Chinese guns towards Zhaocun shell the Japanese field guns; the field guns hit two and drive off the other two.
damaged
The Type 96 company's two modern 15 cm howitzers search the villages east of the town.
17:30: a Chinese night attack forms east of Mengzhuang; the heavy guns break it up.
In the night a Chinese armoured train comes into the station from south of the canal.
06:20: the Japanese guns are ordered onto it.
31 March: the Type 96 company opens on the town's west half.
11:14: nearly all the Japanese artillery, fifteen guns, concentrates on the town, the first of four times before 14:40.
At once more than ten Chinese guns answer on the Japanese batteries at Liujiahu and Sanlizhuang.
15:05: a Chinese battery is found at Canglangmiao, east of the town; it moves on.
15:46: 15 cm-class rounds land on the 3rd Heavy Company and knock out a Type 4 howitzer: the first the Japanese have taken in the battle. They cannot find the guns.
Chinese accounts have the 15 cm guns duelling from 27 March; the Japanese record their first 15 cm-class rounds at 15:46 on 31 March.
damaged
16:15: the Type 96 company fires on a battery it has found at Hanshan.
At 17:12 the China Garrison's independent field-gun company had reported all four of its guns knocked out by Chinese fire.
20:00: under the heavy guns' cover the 11th Company gives up its foothold at the town's north-west corner.
1 April, 01:00: the 10th Field Artillery's commander will not attack under "a superior enemy artillery that has completed its preparations". The attack is put off.
15 cm rounds now fall on Liujiahu and Sanlizhuang five times through the day. The Japanese think they come from towards Xiongshan, but never find the guns.
17:25: the Type 96 company silences guns south of the station.
"Throughout the campaign our artillery hunted the Rheinmetall as its sworn enemy but never caught it" (Ohashi): on retreat the Chinese always got these guns away first.
